LHX.sentence: L3Harris ticked up a touch, but the thing worth watching is that its profit margins are running below where the big defense contractors usually sit — that's the real question mark on this one.

ASML.sentence: ASML is quiet and barely moved — after a big run, next year is expected to be more of a normal recovery year, so the stock isn't stretched the way it looked a while back.

LIN.sentence: Linde is essentially flat and quiet, which is the whole point of this one — it sells oxygen and nitrogen under long contracts and just steadily does its thing.

MSFT.sentence: Microsoft dipped a touch and has actually lagged the other big AI names lately, which can set up a decent entry point, but the cloud-and-AI story just keeps grinding along without drama.

TMO.sentence: Thermo Fisher had a good day, and biotech funding is starting to thaw again — when money flows back into labs, orders for their equipment tend to pick up a couple of quarters later.

ENB.sentence: Enbridge is steady — it runs oil and gas pipelines like a toll road and pays a generous, reliable dividend, which is the main reason to own it.

NOW.sentence: ServiceNow edged up but is still well off its high despite growing fast and outperforming its peers — corporations keep signing on for its workflow and AI automation tools on long contracts.

GLNCY.sentence: Glencore edged up and is paying a hefty dividend — it both mines metals like copper and runs the world's largest commodity trading desk, so it benefits when markets swing.

MLM.sentence: Martin Marietta slipped slightly, but the dip in reported prices is just a quirk of what mix of rock they sold — the real price per ton is still climbing nicely, and this one is not as cheap as the headline numbers make it look.

KOF.sentence: This Latin American Coca-Cola bottler had a mild up day, and the thing that really moves it — the Mexican peso against the dollar — is sitting in normal territory right now.

PBR.A.sentence: Petrobras rose again, and with oil prices well above what it costs them to pump, there's plenty of cash funding its big dividend — though after a strong run it may be due for some profit-taking.

AMKBY.sentence: Maersk, the Danish container-shipping giant, slipped slightly but is trading below what its fleet of ships would cost to replace, which is an unusually cheap level for the company.

MA.sentence: Mastercard was roughly flat and is unusually trading in line with rival Visa rather than at its typical premium — people keep tapping their cards more than ever, so this is more a valuation quirk than a business problem.

ISRG.sentence: No fresh data on the surgical-robot company today, so there's nothing new to report.
